label: Developer tip of the day
items: JSON does not allow trailing commas, comments or single quotes.
Base64 is encoding, not encryption. Never hide secrets with it.
Use SHA-256 for integrity checks and Argon2, scrypt or bcrypt for passwords.
A 10-digit Unix timestamp is seconds; 13 digits is milliseconds.
In a URL, encode each value with encodeURIComponent, not the whole address.
Check colour contrast: text needs at least 4.5:1 against its background for WCAG AA.
A UUID is an identifier, not a secret. Do not use it as a password.
Catastrophic backtracking: avoid nested repetition like (a+)+ in regexes.
401 means "who are you?"; 403 means "I know you, and no".
Use 301 for permanent redirects and 302 for temporary ones so search engines understand.
Hex is handy: two hex digits are exactly one byte.
Long random passwords beat clever short ones; let a manager remember them.
Name the regex groups ((?<year>\d{4})) so your code explains itself.
Store times in UTC and convert to local time only for display.
A 429 response means slow down: honour Retry-After and back off exponentially.
Format JSON before diffing so changes are easy to see.
camelCase for variables, PascalCase for classes, kebab-case for URLs and CSS.
Test regexes with long non-matching strings, not just matching ones.
Sort object keys for stable diffs when logging JSON.
Prefer crypto.getRandomValues over Math.random for anything security related.
The year 2038 problem affects 32-bit signed Unix timestamps.
Read the error message and the line number first; the answer is often right there.
Percent-encoding turns a space into %20, and + only means a space in form data.
Short lines and clear names make code reviewable.
Make a failing test first, then fix the bug, so it stays fixed.
Keep secrets in environment variables or a secrets manager, never in the repo.
Use semantic HTML before ARIA: a real button beats a clickable div.
Minify only for production; keep source maps for debugging.
Rotate API keys you pasted anywhere public, even briefly.
Lorem ipsum is for layout; replace it with real content before launch.
